name: Market pig; deep pit manure mgmt; at farm
description: This unit process represents the production of one market pig in the specified state.  This process includes flows for the material inputs and environmental emissions associated with swine production, at farm. Deep pit manure management is assumed for on site manure handling prior to transport off farm for use. The impacts from different off-farm nutrient management techniques were not included. The applicable classification is ISIC 0145.
category: 11: Agriculture, Forestry, Fishing and Hunting/1122: Hog and Pig Farming

location.name: United States of America, North Carolina

processDocumentation.timeDescription: Data for this project were collected from 2007 through 2014.  Pig production data is based on modeled results and considered to be generally representative of this time period.
processDocumentation.geographyDescription: This unit process represents production in the US Swine Production Region #4, which includes the state of North Carolina.
processDocumentation.technologyDescription: This unit process dataset represents the production of one market pig in a gestation barn using a deep pit to off-farm manure management system, and feed sourced from within the production region specified.  Includes flows for barn infrastructure, swine rations, energy consumption, water consumption, and methane emissions from manure management.  The impacts from different off-farm nutrient management techniques are not included in this process.  Drip or sprinkle cooling and heaters were used for animal temperature regulation.
processDocumentation.inventoryMethodDescription: Life cycle inventory was originally assembled using the SimaPro software platform (Version 8.0.4.26) and was modified for submission using the OpenLCA platform (Version 1.3.0).
processDocumentation.completenessDescription: Includes upstream DataSmart unit processes for the production of electricity, natural gas, and transport, in addition to upstream processes from within this dataset.
processDocumentation.dataSelectionDescription: This is a cradle-to-gate process for the production of market pigs.
processDocumentation.dataTreatmentDescription: The market weight of the pig is assumed to be 275 pounds.  It should be noted that it is not appropriate for the user to assume different market weights when using this dataset.  The LCI data for the production of a market pig in a grow/finish barn were obtained from the University of Arkansas Pig Production Environmental Calculator (PPEC).  The PPEC uses mathematical relationships to simulate swine growth, feed intake and water consumption, electricity and natural gas use, and methane emissions from manure handling during each production cycle, which includes sow, nursery, and grow barns.
processDocumentation.samplingDescription: Flow values used in this project dataset were obtained from a variety of sources, including the 2007 NASS Census of Agriculture and University of Arkansas Pig Production Environmental Calculator (PPEC) process model simulations of the pig production process. The amount of drinking, cooling, and wash water, in addition to rations, natural gas consumption, and other inputs were calculated using the PPEC model.
processDocumentation.dataCollectionDescription: Data for this project was collected from 2007 to 2014. Unit process data were compiled in 2014.

reviews.details: University of Arkansas swine dataset mapped to USLCI technosphere flows and FEDEFL elementary flows for publication on the Federal LCA Commons. Review covers mapping crosswalks, cutoff flows, and export structure.

processDocumentation.intendedApplication: These data may be used in Situation C2, “Accounting without interactions.”  This is applicable to accounting studies that according to their goal definition do not include any interaction with other systems.
processDocumentation.projectDescription: Data were prepared by the University of Arkansas Center for Agricultural and Rural Sustainability for the United States Department of Agriculture National Agriculture Library.  This project was supported in part by the National Pork Board.
